title: Consecutive kth power residues and Erdos 436

problemStatement.formal: IsKthPowerResidue(r,k,p) := \exists a, a^k \equiv r\pmod p;\ AreConsecutiveKthResidues(r,k,m,p) asks r,\ldots,r+m-1 to be kth-power residues, with LambdaFinite(k,m) recording bounded limsup behavior.
problemStatement.plain: Backfill the Erdos 436 metadata around consecutive kth-power residues modulo primes, the formal LambdaFinite interface, checked small lambda values, Hildebrand/Graham-style axiom boundaries, and the remaining odd-k, m=3 problem.
whyMatters: The problem packages a deep distribution question about power residues into finite runs modulo primes.
The Lean development contains useful first-principles residue infrastructure alongside explicitly axiom-backed global theorems.
The metadata needs to keep the solved m=2 direction and the open m=3 odd-k direction separate.

proven: `erdos_436_question1`, `only_small_m_matters`, `quadratic_case_complete`, and `m_2_complete_picture` summarize the formalized solved directions.
open: `lambda_2_2`, `hildebrand_theorem`, `lambda_even_3_infinite`, and `graham_theorem` are axioms in `Erdos436Problem.lean`; the odd-k, m=3 Lambda question remains open.
knownResults.goal: Show the verified power-residue framework and clearly flag the global residue-run theorems that are recorded as axioms.
